newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures close up, helped by cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures close up, helped by cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed slightly higher in lackluster trading, supported by strength in the cash market and firmer natural gas prices, traders said Friday.
"Hopefully we will get the volume cooking again next week after books are cleared and everybody is back from vacation," said one trader.
Sources said recent attention to June and July contracts indicated buyers view those months as undervalued.

Some cited expectations for less early summer runoff for hydroelectric generation given recent wet, warm weather in northern California and the Pacific Northwest, but others said it was still too early to forecast hydropower supplies.
"To tell you the truth, we have a long way to go yet. It is impossible to predict the weather," said one industry source.
February COB closed up 53 cents at $15.85 per megawatt hour (MWh), while March was unchanged at $13.90. Other active COB contracts were up 20 to 70 cents.
February Palo Verde was up 37 cents to $17.00 per MWh, while March was up 2 cents at $15.90. Other PV contracts were 5 to 60 cents higher.
